principle: New original bridge arrangements. Existing source MIDI/native bytes and note streams are untouched. No claim of recovered historical bridge music.

bridges.name: BRIDGE_HOME_CADENCE_TO_CONTEST
bridges.rationale: The HOME ending actually uses Am7, Ab7, Gm7 and C7, with Eb-D-E melody. Its three-note cadential fragment is uniformly condensed by 1/2 into a one-bar connector. C7's E/Bb shell is the common dominant of the two F families; it resolves into unchanged140's Fm7. A 112/116/120 BPM pivot carries the home pocket into the contest grid.

bridges.name: BRIDGE_CONTEST_CMAJ7_C7_TO_HOME
bridges.rationale: The actual contest C-E-E tag over Cmaj7 is followed by its authored C7 turnaround. Cmaj7 admits an Em7 ending as a shared E/G/B upper structure and receives G7 as its local dominant. Lowering only the newly composed shell's B to Bb establishes C7, then the unchanged102 F-major arrival. The source clips finish before this connector's cadential shell; no existing note is shortened.

bridges.name: BRIDGE_CONTEST_C7_TO_HOME
bridges.rationale: The contest's sparse C-E-E cadential tag is newly reharmonized over the already-authored C7 turnaround, without restoring Cmaj7's B-natural. For the middle-section Bb9sus4 ending, C7 is IV-to-V motion toward F. It continues a C7 ending directly and receives the full-cycle Fm7 turnaround as i-to-V before Fmajor. Cadential material is a connector, not a result or KO cue.
